Patch 031 News

This may be the longest period I think officially without an update to A Merchant’s Promise! However, I assure you it has been worked on Full Time (+) all the while.
 

I was pushing hard to get a Beta Patch/Update out this week. but as I play through and adjust, tweak, add, and fix things I would prefer giving a more complete experience than where it is at.

 

YES the map is bigger, yes there are new things, menu updates, swimming, unstuck button, some better performance etc...but I can also see the current stage overall just needs to feel more complete to ensure you are just as excited as I am to see the work that went into it and deliver a more ready to dive in experience.

 

Timeframe wise I don’t plan on dragging it out much longer, but I did just want to stay communicative through the process.

 

Thank you for understanding!

notes.title: Patch 030
notes.notes:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45214938/d6f61357c678750a7d0a0df6099d77f25060ca42.png"]


Patch 030: What you need to know


This patch includes a couple quality of life things such as most Items have their own icons and the Abacus sliders match those icons for easier identification. Also, Abacus slider position should save and when you adjust prices you will see the amount you should get for selling the items appear over them briefly.



While I don't want to rely on UI, players were a little too lost in terms of pricing and this is a compromise for the meantime.



Bigger Note: There are no more boundaries/invisible walls. The map was not designed with this in mind but I did wish to really give this a shot. I'll be updating the map now to accommodate this playstyle.



This has also allowed players to leave their stalls open when leaving town and npc's can still buy their goods.



With these big changes new games may be required more than I would like, so I ADDED an option when starting a new game to continue with your Current Character which allows you to keep your name, money, status.



Here is the full list:


Patch 030 Regular and Beta (synced)(NEW GAME REQUIRED FOR REGULAR (NON BETA USERS)


Improvements:

 Open World style gameplay. Map will be updated to account for this.

 Items now have specific Icons for Food, Drink, Healing, Supplies

 Abacus Sliders match new Item Icons for easier identification

 Abacus Sliders save position

 Changing prices with Abacus results in visual display of New Item Prices

 Villagers can buy your For Sale items while you are gone

 Updated Stamina Icon and Visual Representation

 NPC UI Text no longer blurry

 NPC UI Text changed to not scale (creates effect of conversation further away you must get close to read)

 Testing NPC’s being “live” in all towns

 Updated NPC navigation logic

 Added Option to keep Player Name, Money, Status when starting new game

 Controller navigation to autosave slider in menu

 Removed Giant Transition Walls into Yorlen Harbor and Yorlen Village

 Adjust some sound performance for Player Footsteps



Bug Fixes:

 Floating NPC’s along ground headed to bed position at night

 Not loading saved position on start

 Putting on Shop Wheels for carts

 NPCs not waking up at dawn

 Shop Items being damaged by weather

notes.title: Patch 029 Tomorrow
notes.notes:
Good evening!


Thank you to all those who found the game through the Summer Sale and WELCOME!



I did want to provide and update that I did not meet my goal of getting the Beta Patch 029 out today. 





Firstly....I went ahead and added in an Updated Brake System to the cart that is more visual. 



If you are on the Discord you can see my post here showing it: Cart Brakes



Secondly...while yes the Cart Wheel Replacement system was working as intended....I felt better about changing it to allow for the better goal of:
[olist]
Purchase a wheel

Apply the wheel

Remove the wheel
[/olist]
....all at your discretion and it's the actual wheel, the whole time, no gimmicks. Allowing it to be traded and damaged etc like any other item.



I'll be working hard tomorrow to get Step 3 of that process working and will of course keep you updated!



Apologies for the delay!



As always, I'm in Discord should you need anything.

Patch 028


Because this was a pretty decent Quality of Life implementation I wanted to get it into the Main Game after some quick testing.



As stated, Items (Crates, Boxes etc) will be much more stable when rotating and also have a "feel" of some weight to them. 



Also the boxes performing a check to see if any items are blocking them prior to closing which greatly helps in unnecessary collisions/glitches if you over-fill them.

 Item Rotation/Movement

 Holding Items affects player movement

 Lids check for object prior to closing

notes.title: Looking Good For March Release
notes.notes:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45214938/887194300d3b4cf2b0637840b10b5abf51b56fc5.png

What's the Plan:

For the next few weeks I’ll be working hard to continue adding to the main game.  Sound interactions were Majorly reworked, and items have been reworked as well in effort to allow for as many items to be interacted with as possible.

I am also trying to add in more dynamic environments and life.

Overall I am focusing on 4 areas of the game map for the Initial EA Release. Prison Quarry, Ivernox, Yorlen Village, and Halcyon Harbor. 

And much like the DEMO, after several people get their hands on it I will be bug fixing like mad to get it as solid/stable as possible before starting to add more again.


Performance Matters:

There was a progress delay…if you can call it that…that I self-implemented once I found a way to unlock close to 10-15 FPS for the avg computer. While this may be small for high end comps my goal was to make this as accessible as possible…but it is forcing tedious work redoing literally almost the entire map….it was a hard decision.

All Initial testing is done on a:
12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-12900 3.20 GHz, 80GB Ram
NVIDIA RTX4070
3440x1440 Monitor

I typically see 95+ FPS on Main Game Currently with High/Ultra Settings.


I tested creating more detailed environments (kind of getting away from the low poly look), but the cost was too great as I wanted better than “avg” performance for a open-world-ish Indie game.


I am pushing to be able to rework the Demo some prior to Steam Next Fest. As such I won’t be spending much time Fixing Minor bugs as they may not even be applicable once I bring over more Main Game scripts. However Major or GameBreaking Bugs will be fixed promptly.

Thank you all for being such a great community and I look forward to continuing progress.

I’ll obviously be on the Discord like always but just wanted to give an update.

Demo Progress Continues

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45214938/f13c52187e1a72c86e413544947f74248d527c1a.png

Highlights: Version 0.0.15 

 New Features:   City Magistrates Crime Awareness: Magistrates now track how much the player owes for crime charges. Demo Save Enabled: Saving is now available in the demo, allowing for persistent gameplay. Crime and Trade Stalls: Players must clear crime charges before they can rent a trade stall. Royalty Status Impacted by Item Quality: Selling low-quality items will reduce Royalty Status, while selling quality or exquisite items boosts it. 

 Updates:   Improved item handling to reduce physics-related force glitches. Character movement forces have been improved for smoother control. Stamina management now features a more responsive icon, which flashes when stamina is critical. Improved the handling relationship between the cart and player. Stamina depletion now causes the cart to be automatically released from the player. Various demo map improvements to enhance exploration. Additional graphics options added to the settings menu for better customization. 

 Bug Fixes:   Fixed an issue where holding an item and colliding with heavier objects, like the cart, could cause the entire cart to move. Resolved an issue where the cart would stop too abruptly if the player reversed direction, which sometimes led to unnecessary item damage. Fixed inconsistency in evening lights activating properly when loading the game during evening hours. 

I hope you enjoy these updates and improvements! Hopefully I'll have this Demo to you soon!

notes.title: Weekly Update
notes.notes:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45214938/38e970f169da31dcca1c28e554ac8657dbfc34b9.png

Exciting News: Demo In Progress!

I’m excited to have made the decision to put out a demo! Due to a main aspect of gameplay, specifically the "NO INVENTORY" feature, I can understand players may require time to decide if the gameplay style is for them. I did not feel right eventually putting people on the 2 Hour Steam Refund Window after a purchase. Therefore, I will get a Demo out there focusing on that. It will not be a 1:1 feature match of the actual game, but please take your time and experiment as much as you like!

This release will feature two demo cities where you can experience a glimpse of the A Merchant's Promise world. Your feedback is incredibly valuable as I continue to refine the game, so please dive in and let me know what you think when it releases!


Version 0.0.14 Update Summary:

 Wheel Controller Upgrade: Moved away from Unity Wheel Colliders and implemented a new Wheel Controller for improved performance and reliability. New Demo Scene: Added a new demo scene featuring two demo cities and roads. (Scene and component setup was the main focus this week!) Random Item Spawning: Working on implementing random item spawn for villager houses, so each game load presents different items. Crime System Update: Trying to eat food without purchasing it or stealing food from trader areas now triggers a crime (improved implementation). NPC Dialogue Speed: NPC text dialogue speed has been doubled. Tutorial Additions: Added tutorial text to certain objects to assist new players. Hunger/Thirst System Overhaul: Eating and drinking now provide instant recovery based on food/drink quality. Hunger and thirst contribute to a stamina recovery modifier that boosts how fast you recover stamina, impacting future speed. 

Bug Fixes:  Performance Improvements: Fixed lag caused by lots of damaged items breaking. Processing time was reduced from 18ms (high lag) to 2.1ms (no lag) by redrawing colliders and adjusting gravity/collision for fragmented objects. NPC Interaction Bug: Pressing "E" while talking to a character no longer causes their model to blink in and out of existence. Discord Link Fix: The Discord link in the welcome message is now clickable.

notes.title: Weekly Update
notes.notes:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45214938/84e90f09290c219b0948a38f8d3f4ac674b850de.png

Villager AI Evolution

- Villagers now have basic needs like Drinking, Eating, and Sleeping, adding more life and realism to their daily routines. You'll see them move purposefully through town, visiting local spots and interacting more naturally with their environment. Shortly to come they should also have a new goal: traveling between cities and villages, creating more dynamic movement across the game world.

Animations

- While just placeholders for now...I've introduced them to ensure the logic behind animations is functioning correctly. This groundwork will make it easy to swap in more polished animations later, while giving villagers some life-like actions for now. Though watching them float around was kind of funny.

- Save System Improvements: Performance optimizations have been made to the save system, providing a smoother and faster save/load experience.

Great Results for Stress Test

- I was very happy that the AI coding for the NPC's ran pretty well. While their current tasks are still simple I was able to maintain 95+ FPS even with nearly 200 active NPC's running around a singular village. (For reference there will ever only be a few dozen active at one time as the ones you don't see are placed into a dormant state or not rendered).

Bug Fixes

- Fixed a large FPS drop that occurred when several villagers tried to buy items from the player. The system is now optimized to keep gameplay smooth during busy moments.

- Addressed a critical issue with item and player position consistency during loading. Items and characters will now appear exactly where they were saved, ensuring continuity without frustrating misplacements. This was little tricky due to everything being "physics" based but it's now working properly. These updates are just a glimpse of the exciting progress as I continue to bring more life and detail to your medieval world. Thank you for being part of this journey!

New Feature Highlight
King's Road Tolls and Crime Update

Previously, if the player committed a crime, such as stealing, it would only affect the player's relationship with the faction of that Shopkeeper. This week, I've made improvements to that system.

New "Charges" Stat
The Player now has a "Charges" stat, which acts as a bounty. This stat increases every time the Player commits a crime. In addition to this, committing crimes still negatively affects the Player's relationship with the applicable Faction. But don’t worry—the Player can pay off their Charges.

King's Road Tolls
I've also introduced a basic Toll for traveling the King's Road. Pay the toll to save time on your journey, or take the back roads to avoid it. But be warned:
Entering the King's Road without payment will result in your crime being reported, your Charges increasing, and your standing with the Royal Family being negatively affected.

This system will continue to evolve and improve over time.

Thank you for your continued support!
